routes.label: Count each digit in each position

question: What is the average (mean) of all \(5\)-digit numbers that can be formed by using each of the digits \(1,\) \(3,\) \(5,\) \(7,\) and \(8\) exactly once?
solution:
Every digit appears equally often in each position. To see why, fix a digit in one position. The remaining four digits can fill the other positions in
\[
4\cdot3\cdot2\cdot1=24
\]
ways. Each arrangement is counted once because its successive digits determine all four choices. There are therefore \(5\cdot24=120\) numbers overall, and each digit occurs \(24\) times in each position.

The digit sum is \(1+3+5+7+8=24\). Thus the sum of the digits in any one position across all the numbers is \(24\cdot24\). Applying the place values gives
\[
\text{total sum}=24\cdot24\cdot11111,
\]
since \(10000+1000+100+10+1=11111\). Consequently,
\[
\text{mean}
=\frac{24\cdot24\cdot11111}{120}
=\frac{24}{5}\cdot11111
=53332.8.
\]
The answer is \(53332.8\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
Group a number with the four numbers obtained by repeatedly moving its first digit to the end. All five numbers remain valid five-digit numbers because none of the digits is zero. They are distinct because their first digits are distinct.

These groups partition all the numbers: every number belongs to a group, and rotating any member produces exactly the same five members, so two groups cannot partly overlap.

Within each group, every digit appears once in each position. The sum of the five numbers is therefore
\[
(1+3+5+7+8)(10000+1000+100+10+1)
=24\cdot11111.
\]
Every group has mean
\[
\frac{24\cdot11111}{5}=53332.8.
\]
Combining groups with this same mean leaves the overall mean unchanged. The answer is \(53332.8\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutionMethods.label: Average groups of five rotations
